manifest.name: Clusters
manifest.description: The cluster inventory: switch the active cluster; administrators add clusters and set their environment and read-only flag.

table.emptyAdminHint: Add a cluster with its kubeconfig to get started.
table.emptyUserHint: An administrator has not given you access to a cluster yet.

readOnly.label: Read-only
readOnly.hint: Changes and shell access are blocked for everyone on this cluster, administrators included.

actions.activateHint: Switch to this cluster; the workbench reloads.
actions.bookmarkHint: Entries added by address are bookmarks without credentials and cannot be activated.

note.live: The KubeBench server keeps each kubeconfig in its own database; clusters added by address only are bookmarks.
note.mock: Demo mode: the inventory is kept in this browser and every entry shows the same sample data.

remove.title: Remove {{name}}?
remove.message: KubeBench forgets the cluster: its stored credentials and the users' access to it are deleted. The cluster itself is not changed.
remove.messageActive: This is the active cluster. KubeBench forgets it — its stored credentials and the users' access to it are deleted — and switches to another cluster. The cluster itself is not changed.

form.name: Name
form.environmentHelp: Production clusters get a red status bar and ask for the resource name before destructive actions.
form.readOnlyHelp: Blocks changes and shell access for everyone, administrators included. Reading stays possible.

errors.name: Enter a name of 1 to {{max}} characters.
errors.nameTaken: A cluster with this name already exists.
errors.content: Paste the kubeconfig or load it from a file.
errors.path: Enter the path of the kubeconfig file on the server.
errors.address: Enter an http:// or https:// address.
errors.fileTooLarge: {{name}} is too large to be a kubeconfig.

add.title: Add cluster
add.nameHelp: How the cluster is shown in KubeBench.

sourceHelp.content: The server stores the kubeconfig. Embed certificates and tokens in it: references to files or credential plugins may not be allowed. The EKS, GKE and AKS plugins are: KubeBench signs in to them itself.
sourceHelp.path: The server reads the file once and stores its contents.
sourceHelp.address: Only remembers the address; KubeBench cannot connect to a bookmark.

add.contextHelp: Leave empty to use the kubeconfig's current context.

platform.unknownHint: Detected once someone connects to the cluster.

help.keep: The stored {{provider}} credentials stay as they are. They are never shown again.
help.server: EKS, GKE and AKS kubeconfigs sign in with the KubeBench server's own cloud identity (pod or VM identity, environment). Other kubeconfigs use their own credentials.
help.aws-keys: An IAM access key, for a kubeconfig that runs aws eks get-token or aws-iam-authenticator. Stored with the cluster and never shown again.
help.aws-profile: A profile from the AWS configuration files of the KubeBench server.
help.gcp: A service-account key file (JSON), for a kubeconfig that uses gke-gcloud-auth-plugin. Stored with the cluster and never shown again.
help.azure: A service principal with a client secret, for a kubeconfig that uses kubelogin. Stored with the cluster and never shown again.

errors.profile: Enter a profile name (letters, digits and _.+=,@-).
errors.serviceAccount: Paste a service-account key: JSON with "type": "service_account".
errors.fileTooLarge: {{name}} is too large to be a service-account key.
